issue.title: Simplify UI Effects controls to Off / Tactile
issue.description:
Simplify the existing UI Effects controls so the user chooses only whether the effect is Off or Tactile, while the supported targets are handled automatically by the effect recipe.

## Overall direction

The current UI Effects section exposes:

* Effect: Tactile
* Secondary buttons toggle
* Tabs toggle
* Strength

This is more configuration than needed for the current feature.

Simplify the control model to:

* Effect dropdown/select
  * Off
  * Tactile
* short helper text explaining what Tactile affects
* shared Strength control

Remove the independent Secondary buttons and Tabs toggles.

## 1. Effect options

Update the Effect select so it contains:

* Off
* Tactile

Default:

* Off

Behavior:

### Off

* no tactile styling is applied;
* Secondary Buttons remain flat;
* surface/pill-style Tabs remain flat;
* Strength is disabled, muted, or otherwise clearly non-interactive;
* existing flat appearance is preserved.

### Tactile

* automatically applies the accepted tactile treatment to:
  * Secondary Buttons
  * active surface/pill-style Tabs
* line/minimal Tabs remain excluded;
* all non-secondary Button variants remain flat;
* Strength becomes active and controls the shared tactile intensity.

Do not require separate target toggles.

## 2. Remove target toggles

Remove the existing UI controls for:

* Secondary buttons
* Tabs

Do not replace them with another per-target configuration mechanism in this ticket.

The effect recipe itself owns its supported targets.

## 3. Add concise helper text

Add a small helper note under or near the Effect control.

Suggested copy:

`Affects Secondary buttons and surface-style Tabs.`

Equivalent wording is acceptable if clearer, but keep it concise.

Do not turn this into a long explanatory block.

## 4. Strength behavior

Preserve the existing shared Strength control.

Requirements:

* Strength remains the single bounded control for tactile intensity;
* when Effect = Off, Strength is disabled or visually de-emphasized;
* when Effect = Tactile, Strength becomes active;
* preserve current tactile visual behavior and tuning unless a tiny adjustment is required by the simplified state model.

Do not introduce additional raw effect controls.

## 5. Theme/state simplification

Prefer simplifying persisted UI Effects state from a target-toggle model toward a smaller effect model.

Conceptually:

`effect: "off" | "tactile"`
`strength: number`

The exact implementation should follow the accepted Theme v3 schema conventions.

Backward compatibility requirements:

* older themes with no UI Effects value resolve to Off;
* themes from the current toggle-based implementation continue to import safely;
* if a previously saved theme had Tactile enabled for either accepted target, reconcile it deterministically to the new Tactile state without corrupting unrelated theme data;
* if a previously saved theme had no active tactile target, reconcile to Off;
* newly exported themes preserve Effect and Strength;
* do not introduce Theme v4 solely for this simplification unless source inspection proves the existing Theme v3 contract cannot support the migration safely.

If the current accepted persisted schema makes this a public schema/mutation change, classify and verify it accordingly rather than hiding the contract change.

## 6. Effect target semantics

The supported targets remain fixed for the Tactile effect:

* Secondary Button
* active surface/pill-style Tabs

Explicitly preserve exclusions:

* default/primary Buttons
* outline Buttons
* destructive Buttons
* ghost Buttons
* link Buttons
* line/minimal Tabs
* Inputs
* all other primitives

Do not broaden tactile coverage in this ticket.

## 7. Visual behavior

Preserve the accepted tactile visual direction:

* subtle tactile illumination;
* soft internal light/wash;
* restrained edge definition;
* minimal obvious drop shadow;
* clean, modern, understated;
* no heavy glossy/beveled/retro treatment.

Secondary Buttons are the preferred tactile target because they provide a filled neutral surface. The tactile treatment may add subtle ring/edge definition without competing with the built-in border semantics of Outline Buttons.

This ticket is primarily a control/state simplification, not a visual redesign.

## 8. Accessibility and interaction

* Effect select remains keyboard accessible;
* Strength disabled state is semantically and visually clear when Off;
* focus-visible behavior remains intact;
* light/dark behavior remains correct;
* no regression to Button or Tabs keyboard/selected/disabled semantics.

## 9. Boundaries

Do not:

* add new effect families;
* add new targets;
* reintroduce per-target toggles elsewhere;
* add tactile Inputs;
* change public Button/Tabs APIs;
* add dependencies;
* add network behavior;
* redesign unrelated Effects controls;
* change Shadow or Motion behavior.

Preserve:

* Theme v3 where safely possible;
* history;
* dirty state;
* reset behavior;
* import/export;
* Design Command behavior unless the accepted closed mutation schema requires a narrow corresponding update;
* public registry;
* current tactile visual language.

## Acceptance

* UI Effects Effect select contains Off and Tactile.
* Off is the backward-compatible default.
* Secondary buttons toggle is removed.
* Tabs toggle is removed.
* A concise helper note explains that Tactile affects Secondary buttons and surface-style Tabs.
* Effect = Tactile automatically applies the effect to the accepted Secondary Button and active surface-style Tabs targets.
* Outline and all other previously excluded Button variants remain flat.
* Strength is disabled/de-emphasized when Off and active when Tactile.
* Existing tactile visual language remains materially unchanged while moving the Button target from Outline to Secondary.
* Older/no-effect themes remain visually flat.
* Existing toggle-based saved themes import/reconcile safely.
* Newly exported themes preserve Effect and Strength.
* No Theme v4, new dependency, network behavior, target expansion, or unrelated UI change is introduced unless strictly required by the accepted schema contract.
